BIE task prefix understand.read_page/3 · rulebook canvas_profile@2026-10-27.1+content_types@2026-10-24.1+explanations@2026-10-24.1+level_profiles@2026-10-24.1+simple_hindi@2026-10-25.1+teacher_examples@2026-10-24.1+vision-2026-10-21@2026-10-21.13+visual_grammar@2026-10-26.2+visual_levels@2026-10-26.2 · content types 2026-10-24.1 · schema bie.brain.understand-page/3

You are BIE's book-understanding section: an expert teacher of Indian Economy for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS.
You read one page of a book chapter with two eyes, the page's native text blocks and the page image, and turn it into a complete,
question-based teacher's understanding. Later BIE sections build the video lessons, the chapter game and the notes only from what you
capture, so anything you miss is missing from the whole course. Your output is internal to BIE: write it in clear English and keep the
book's own terms and spellings.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S1-01] Read the page with two eyes: the native text blocks (exact words and numbers) and the page image (tables, diagrams, labels, arrows, equations, layout). Items that exist only in the image are as important as text items. A page whose text layer is empty or nearly empty is read entirely from the image.
[S1-02] Every native text block is either covered by an item (its id in that item's block_ids) or listed as boilerplate. Boilerplate is only running headers, page numbers, publisher adverts, contact lines and watermarks; nothing teachable is boilerplate.
[S1-03] Every table becomes one 'table' item plus one 'table_row' item per row, in order, each row's content giving every cell with its column header, for example 'Smooth muscle | Location: G.I. tract, uterus, eye, blood vessels | Function: peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size, erects hairs | Appearance: no striations, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary'. A table continued from the previous page continues the same table.
[S1-04] Every diagram, chart, flow or tree becomes one 'diagram' item that says what it shows and how its parts connect (arrows, branches, flows, sequence), plus one 'diagram_label' item per label naming what the label points to. A classification tree lists every branch and leaf with its parent.
[S1-05] Every equation, formula, chemical formula and symbol is read exactly and each symbol's meaning and unit are stated.
[S1-06] Understand every teachable item by questioning it like a teacher. Ask the questions that fit: what is it, what is it about, where does it apply or occur, how does it work, when, who and whom, which, why, how does it compare, how does it differ, what is the evidence, what are the exceptions, what follows from it. Then keep asking 'why' and 'how' on your own answers (depth 2, 3 ...) until a teacher could explain it to a student meeting it for the first time. Answers explain; they never just repeat the item's words.
[S1-07] Mark every answer's basis: 'book' only when the page itself states it, 'outside' when any part comes from general knowledge. Use outside knowledge to make the book understandable (mechanisms, reasons, real-life links), never to change what the book says. Keep outside explanations at standard textbook level for these learners and avoid absolute words (always, only, never, all, every) unless the book uses them.
[S1-08] Give every item its true content type, one of BIE's nine: process, structure, classification, comparison, timeline, cause_effect, facts_numbers, figure, definition (bie/brain/rulebook/content_types.json). An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a question or an answer option is a role, not a type. BIE's code proposes a type before you read the page; when you choose another, say why. The content type decides the required questions and later how the lesson teaches it, how the video shows it, how the game makes it playable and how the notes draw it, so choose by what the content is, not by how it is printed.
[S1-09] Name the prerequisites a student must already understand for each item, as concrete concepts ('cell and its nucleus', 'what a nerve impulse is'), never vague ('basic biology'). Prerequisites are taught later, not just listed.
[S1-10] Judge exam importance for the course's exam (for UPSC / State PCS: classifications, comparisons, locations, functions, examples and odd-one-out facts are high). Every previous-year or practice question on the page is captured with its options and linked to the items it tests.
[S1-11] Where the text layer and the image disagree (garbled symbols, missing words, wrong order), report the disagreement. Trust the image for symbols, layout and diagrams, and the text layer for spelling when it is clean.
[S1-13] A printed typo stays as printed, with the right word after it in square brackets: 'Cartiage [Cartilage]' (Navin, 23 October 2026). The teacher answers use the right word. Never correct the book silently.
[S1-14] One answer, one basis (Navin, 23 October 2026): an answer that would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one with basis 'book' (only what the page states) and one with basis 'outside'.
[S1-15] Open every teachable item for the learner (Navin, 24 October 2026): in unpack, the terms the learner must hold (each with its plain meaning in simple Hindi and one everyday image), a why chain of 1-4 steps that starts from a need or a problem (each step names its basis, book or standard), an example or the place where it is seen, the consequence, the visual verb the video should show, and what the level profile adds. Every teachable item has at least one unpack element; an unpack that only restates the item in other words is empty.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a read_page card:
- card.parts: BIE's code has already proposed a content type for groups of this page's native text blocks (item_ids are block ids;
  "pNNNN-image" is the page image), with the evidence in "focus". It is a proposal from keywords and patterns, not a verdict: give
  every item its true type (S1-08). When you choose another type than BIE's proposal for an item's blocks, say why in one line in that
  item's type_note; BIE's code compares every item and sends unexplained differences back to you.
- card.coverage: every id in must_cover must be in some item's block_ids or in boilerplate_block_ids; may_skip lists blocks BIE thinks are
  running headers or page numbers. Never list an id that is not on this page.
- card.context.before and after: one line from the previous and the next page, for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,
  your main decisions (how you split items, how you read an unclear part, a type you chose against BIE's proposal) with a reason each,
  and what is uncertain.
- items: everything on the page, in reading order.
  - item_id: short and unique on this page ("i1", "i2", ...).
  - kind: heading, paragraph, definition, list_point, example, table (the whole table), table_row (one per row), diagram (the whole figure),
    diagram_label (one per label), equation, symbol, box_note, caption, question (a PYQ or practice question), answer_option, other.
  - parent_item_id: the table of a table_row, the diagram of a diagram_label, the question of an answer_option, else "". When the page
    starts with the options of a question printed on the previous page, add one question item for that question (content: "continued
    from the previous page" and what the options answer) and make it their parent.
  - source: "text" if the item comes from native text blocks, "image" if it is visible only in the image, "both" if both show it.
  - block_ids: the ids of the native text blocks this item covers ([] for image-only items). Use only ids from the card.
  - where_on_page: where it is ("top table, row 2", "right diagram, label at the axon end").
  - content: the exact words for text items; a complete, faithful reading for image items (every cell with its column header for a
    table_row; what a label names and what it points to for a diagram_label; all branches for a tree). A printed typo stays as
    printed with the right word after it in square brackets, "Cartiage [Cartilage]" (S1-13); never correct the book silently.
  - content_type: one of BIE's nine type ids above, by what the content is. An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a table
    row or a diagram label usually takes its table's or diagram's type. "none" only for a question, an answer option or an item that is
    not teachable.
  - type_note: "" when you agree with BIE's proposal for this item's blocks (or there is none); otherwise one line on why your type fits.
  - teachable: false only for pure headings and containers whose children carry the content.
  - teacher_understanding: the teacher's questions and answers for this item (S1-06); depth 1 for first questions, 2 and more for
    "why"/"how" on an earlier answer; basis "book" only if the page states it, else "outside"; one answer, one basis: an answer that
    would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one "book" and one "outside" (S1-14). BIE's code
    checks every teachable item:
    at least two questions, at least one "why" or "how", at least the required questions of its content type, and no answer that only
    repeats its question or the item's words.
  - prerequisites: concrete concepts a student must understand first.
  - exam_importance and exam_note: for this exam.
  - tests_item_ids: for a question, the ids on this page that it tests ([] if they are on other pages).
  - unpack: how a teacher opens this book line for the learner (S1-15; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, never a
    reader of the line). For every teachable item, at the depth of the level profile below:
    terms = the words of the line the learner must own: [{term (as the book spells it), plain_meaning (everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari
    with the book's English terms in Roman: "tissue", "cell", "epithelium", "muscle", never their textbook Hindi ऊतक, कोशिका, उपकला, मांसपेशी;
    BIE's code sends an item back for a textbook translation. For example "absorptive surface" → "जहाँ चीज़ें अंदर ली जाती हैं"),
    everyday_image (one image from the learner's
    home or body: "आँत खाने के पोषक तत्व सोखती है, जैसे कागज़ पानी")}]; why_chain = the why in steps, starting from a need or a
    problem ("पेट में HCl बनता है, इसलिए अंदर एक lining चाहिए"), each step with its basis: "book" when the page says it, "standard"
    when it is standard textbook knowledge; example_or_place = one example, or the place by a zoom from the organ the learner knows;
    consequence = what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea of the page; visual_verb = what visibly happens on the
    screen when this is taught ("particles cross the thin layer"); level_extra = what this level adds (the other names, the exam's
    trap, the memory trick) or "". BIE's code checks that every teachable item has at least one unpack element and that every why
    step names its basis; a locked explanation given with the source is reused as it is. A question item or a pure heading leaves
    unpack empty.
- boilerplate_block_ids: ids of running headers, page numbers, adverts, contact lines and watermarks only.
- text_image_disagreements: where the text layer and the image differ.
Reply with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

p0015-b0001 | Indian Economy
p0015-b0002 |  Enables banking transactions using Aadhaar and biometrics, primarily for financial
p0015-b0003 | inclusion.
p0015-b0004 |  Authentication and payment is done via Bank Mitras.

p0015-b0007 | 2. BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System)
p0015-b0008 |  Provides a single interoperable platform for paying bills such as electricity, mobile,

p0015-b0010 | NPCI manages both AEPS and BBPS.
p0015-b0011 | Rupay Card Payment Gateway (2012)
p0015-b0012 | • Rupee + Payment = RuPay card . It was launched by NPCI.
p0015-b0013 | • It is world’s 7th payment gateway similar to Mastercard, Visacard,
p0015-b0014 | China’s Union Pay.
p0015-b0015 | • Rupay charges less fees than other companies and is India’s
p0015-b0016 | domestic payment system.
p0015-b0017 | • Types of Cards: RuPay debit, credit, and prepaid cards.
p0015-b0018 | • Rupay debit card given free with PMJDY (Jan Dhan) Bank account.
p0015-b0019 | • One of India's major payment innovations is linking RuPay Credit
p0015-b0020 | Cards to UPI.
p0015-b0021 | E-Rupi by NPCI (2021)
p0015-b0022 | • E-Rupi is an SMS /QR Code based Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher created by
p0015-b0023 | National Payment Corporation of India (NPCI) using its UPI Platform.
p0015-b0024 | • It is not a payment app, bank transfer, or digital currency.
p0015-b0025 | • Instead, it is a person-specific and purpose-specific voucher that can only be used by the
p0015-b0026 | intended beneficiary for the intended service.

output.page_summary: AEPS uses Aadhaar and biometrics through Bank Mitras; BBPS offers interoperable bill payments. NPCI manages both. RuPay is presented as India's domestic card payment system, launched in 2012, with debit, credit and prepaid cards and selected overseas acceptance. E-Rupi, introduced in 2021, is an SMS/QR-based prepaid voucher restricted to an intended person and service.

items.content: Enables banking transactions using Aadhaar and biometrics, primarily for financial inclusion.

teacher_understanding.question: How does AEPS identify a user for banking transactions?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies Aadhaar and biometrics as the means used for transactions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can this support financial inclusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Biometric identity verification at a nearby service point can reduce dependence on travelling to a branch or using a card and PIN, helping people access banking services.

items.exam_note: Associate AEPS with Aadhaar and biometrics, not with a bill-payment platform.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की पहचान वाली खासियत से पहचान जाँचना
terms.everyday_image: fingerprint देकर पहचान की जाँच

terms.plain_meaning: जिन लोगों तक banking नहीं पहुँचती, उन्हें भी उससे जोड़ना
terms.everyday_image: गाँव के व्यक्ति को पास में banking सुविधा मिलना

why_chain.step: Some people face distance and access barriers to banking.
AEPS uses Aadhaar and biometrics primarily to support financial inclusion.

unpack.example_or_place: A village resident using an Aadhaar-enabled banking service point.
unpack.consequence: Connect identity verification with access to banking, then locate the Bank Mitra's role.
unpack.visual_verb: verify identity and open access
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish identity authentication from the source of money in an account.

items.content: Authentication and payment is done via Bank Mitras.

teacher_understanding.question: How are AEPS authentication and payment accessed according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are carried out through Bank Mitras, who provide the local service interface.

teacher_understanding.question: When does authentication matter in this service?
teacher_understanding.answer: Identity is checked when the customer requests a transaction, before the transaction is authorised.

teacher_understanding.question: Why use a Bank Mitra rather than require a branch visit?
teacher_understanding.answer: A bank's local representative can bring assisted banking closer to people who have difficulty reaching or using a branch.

items.exam_note: Bank Mitra is the service intermediary; do not confuse the intermediary with NPCI.

terms.plain_meaning: bank की ओर से लोगों को पास में banking सेवा देने वाले प्रतिनिधि
terms.everyday_image: गाँव की दुकान पर banking सहायता का counter

why_chain.step: A distant branch can make routine banking difficult.
Bank Mitras provide the authentication and payment interface described here.

unpack.example_or_place: An assisted transaction at a local Bank Mitra point.
unpack.consequence: Financial inclusion requires a usable local access point as well as an identity system.
unpack.visual_verb: connect customer to bank through an agent
unpack.level_extra: Keep the customer-facing agent distinct from the payment-system operator.

items.content: Helps in Direct Benefits Transfer, helping government subsidies reach the grassroots levels.

teacher_understanding.question: How is AEPS linked to subsidy delivery?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says it supports Direct Benefits Transfer and helps government subsidies reach grassroots beneficiaries.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does access to banking matter after a benefit has been transferred?
teacher_understanding.answer: A credit in an account is useful only if the recipient can access or use it; a nearby assisted banking point can help bridge this last-mile gap.

items.exam_note: Distinguish DBT as benefit delivery from AEPS as a banking-access mechanism.

terms.plain_meaning: सरकार का लाभ सीधे लाभ पाने वाले तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: सरकारी मदद की रकम beneficiary के account में पहुँचना

why_chain.step: A beneficiary needs practical access to a government benefit, not merely an account entry.
AEPS helps government subsidies reach grassroots levels.

unpack.example_or_place: A beneficiary accessing a credited subsidy through a local banking point.
unpack.consequence: Links payment infrastructure to welfare implementation.
unpack.visual_verb: trace benefit to beneficiary
unpack.level_extra: Do not describe AEPS itself as a subsidy scheme.

items.content: 2. BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System)
items.exam_note: Expansion is developed in the following item.

items.content: Provides a single interoperable platform for paying bills such as electricity, mobile, gas, insurance, etc.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Bharat Bill Payment System provide?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides a common interoperable platform for paying different kinds of bills, including electricity, mobile, gas and insurance.

teacher_understanding.question: Which examples show that BBPS is not limited to one utility?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page lists electricity, mobile, gas and insurance bills.

teacher_understanding.question: How does interoperability help the payer?
teacher_understanding.answer: Participating billers and payment channels can work through common arrangements, reducing the need for an isolated payment route for each biller.

items.exam_note: Interoperable bill payments are the defining clue; the examples are not an exhaustive list.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग जुड़े systems का आपस में काम कर पाना
terms.everyday_image: एक payment रास्ते से अलग-अलग bill भरना

why_chain.step: Households have bills from several different providers.
BBPS brings multiple bill categories onto a single interoperable platform.

unpack.example_or_place: Paying electricity and mobile bills through a participating payment channel.
unpack.consequence: Separates bill-payment infrastructure from AEPS identity-based banking access.
unpack.visual_verb: converge several bills onto one platform
unpack.level_extra: A common platform does not mean that there is only one customer-facing app.

items.content: NPCI manages both AEPS and BBPS.

teacher_understanding.question: Which common institution manages the two systems named here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page attributes management of both AEPS and BBPS to NPCI.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the page's explicit institutional link between AEPS and BBPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: A separate bold sentence states that NPCI manages both.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should common management not make a student treat them as the same service?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their functions on the page differ: AEPS supports Aadhaar-biometric banking, while BBPS supports interoperable bill payments.

items.exam_note: Useful institution–product matching fact; retain the page's management wording.

terms.plain_meaning: कई payment systems से जुड़ी संस्था
terms.everyday_image: एक संस्था के नीचे अलग-अलग काम करने वाले payment रास्ते

why_chain.step: Different payment needs require different systems.
The page gives AEPS and BBPS a common manager, NPCI.

unpack.example_or_place: An institution–system matching question.
unpack.consequence: Introduces the same institution before RuPay and e-RUPI.
unpack.visual_verb: branch NPCI into two named systems
unpack.level_extra: Common institutional parent does not imply identical purpose.

items.content: Rupay Card Payment Gateway (2012)

teacher_understanding.question: Which year does the page associate with RuPay's introduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heading gives 2012.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a domestic card payment system significant?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides a domestic card-network option rather than leaving card payments dependent solely on foreign networks.

items.exam_note: Link RuPay to 2012; the book uses 'payment gateway' terminology.

why_chain.step: Card payments need a network connecting participating institutions.
The page places RuPay's introduction in 2012 and describes it as domestic.

unpack.example_or_place: A RuPay-branded bank card.
unpack.consequence: Anchors the later product features in time.
unpack.visual_verb: place RuPay at 2012
unpack.level_extra: Outside clarification: RuPay is a card payment network; 'network' and a merchant payment gateway are not technically identical.

items.content: Rupee + Payment = RuPay card. It was launched by NPCI.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the name RuPay combine, and who launched it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page combines Rupee and Payment to explain the name and identifies NPCI as the launcher.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the plus-and-equals expression establish?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the page's name mnemonic, not a numerical payment formula.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the mnemonic be used in an exam?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use it to remember the brand, while keeping the institution–product link, NPCI–RuPay, separate from the wordplay.

items.exam_note: NPCI–RuPay matching is more important than the name mnemonic.

why_chain.step: A brand name needs to be linked to its institution.
The page supplies both the Rupee–Payment mnemonic and NPCI as launcher.

unpack.example_or_place: NPCI → RuPay on a revision chart.
unpack.consequence: Connects RuPay to the institutional theme of the page.
unpack.visual_verb: join Rupee and Payment into RuPay
unpack.level_extra: The symbols + and = indicate word combination here; they have no units.

items.content: It is world’s 7th payment gateway similar to Mastercard, Visacard [Visa card], China’s Union Pay.

teacher_understanding.question: Which systems does the page compare with RuPay?
teacher_understanding.answer: It places RuPay alongside Mastercard, Visa and China's Union Pay as similar payment systems, while calling RuPay the world's seventh payment gateway.

teacher_understanding.question: What domestic identity distinguishes RuPay in the adjacent text?
teacher_understanding.answer: The next bullet identifies RuPay specifically as India's domestic payment system.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the seventh-place description be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: As an attributed book claim, not as proof of a current ranking by transaction volume, size or quality; this page supplies no such criterion.

items.exam_note: Retain the named comparators; avoid turning an unsupported ordinal into a current market-share ranking.

why_chain.step: Students need familiar comparators to identify RuPay's role.
The page compares it with Mastercard, Visa and Union Pay.

unpack.example_or_place: Different network logos printed on bank cards.
unpack.consequence: Places RuPay in the card-payment family, not among currencies.
unpack.visual_verb: align card-network logos
unpack.level_extra: The book's gateway wording is broader than the technical card-network distinction.

items.content: Rupay charges less fees than other companies and is India’s domestic payment system.

teacher_understanding.question: What fee comparison does the book make?
teacher_understanding.answer: It says RuPay charges lower fees than other companies, without specifying the fee category or amount.

teacher_understanding.question: What national identity does the page assign RuPay?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes RuPay as India's domestic payment system.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can lower payment-processing costs matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: They can reduce the cost burden of accepting and processing electronic payments and encourage participation.

items.exam_note: Lower fees do not mean all transactions and cards are free.

terms.plain_meaning: अपने देश का payment system
terms.everyday_image: भारत के bank card पर RuPay का निशान

why_chain.step: Payment services involve processing costs.
The book presents RuPay as a lower-fee domestic option.

unpack.example_or_place: Merchant card acceptance and bank card processing.
unpack.consequence: Explains the economic relevance of the domestic-system claim.
unpack.visual_verb: compare fee bars
unpack.level_extra: No numeric fee, fee payer or universal zero-fee rule is stated.

items.content: Types of Cards: RuPay debit, credit, and prepaid cards.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three RuPay card types are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Debit, credit and prepaid cards.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these types differ by source of spending funds?
teacher_understanding.answer: Debit generally draws on account funds; credit uses an approved borrowing limit repaid later; prepaid uses value loaded in advance.

teacher_understanding.question: How can all three still be RuPay cards?
teacher_understanding.answer: The network brand and the funding arrangement are separate dimensions: the same network can support different card products.

items.exam_note: Reject the statement that RuPay is exclusively a debit card.

terms.plain_meaning: खर्च का पैसा अपने account से कटता है
terms.everyday_image: खरीदारी के बाद bank balance कम होना

terms.plain_meaning: अभी उधार की limit से खर्च, बाद में चुकाना
terms.everyday_image: महीने के अंत में card bill भरना

terms.plain_meaning: पहले से भरी रकम से खर्च करना
terms.everyday_image: पहले recharge, फिर इस्तेमाल

why_chain.step: People may pay from savings, borrowing or preloaded value.
RuPay includes debit, credit and prepaid cards.

unpack.example_or_place: Compare account balance, credit limit and loaded value.
unpack.consequence: Prepares learners to distinguish the PMJDY debit-card point from RuPay credit-card linkage.
unpack.visual_verb: split RuPay into three funding types
unpack.level_extra: Classify by source of funds, not by the shared network logo.

items.content: Rupay debit card given free with PMJDY (Jan Dhan) Bank account.

teacher_understanding.question: Which card is associated with a Jan Dhan account here?
teacher_understanding.answer: A RuPay debit card, described as given free with the PMJDY account.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the page promise a free RuPay credit card with PMJDY?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. The specific product named is a debit card.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can a debit card help turn account ownership into usable access?
teacher_understanding.answer: It gives the account holder a way to access account funds through supported card facilities rather than relying solely on branch counters.

items.exam_note: The trap is replacing 'debit' with 'credit' or reading free card provision as free money.

terms.plain_meaning: लोगों को banking से जोड़ने वाली Jan Dhan account योजना
terms.everyday_image: नए account के साथ RuPay debit card मिलना

why_chain.step: Opening an account should be followed by ways to use its funds.
The page links a free RuPay debit card to Jan Dhan accounts.

unpack.example_or_place: A Jan Dhan account holder's RuPay debit card.
unpack.consequence: Connects RuPay to the financial-inclusion theme introduced through AEPS.
unpack.visual_verb: attach debit card to Jan Dhan account
unpack.level_extra: PMJDY expands to Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (outside clarification).

items.content: One of India's major payment innovations is linking RuPay Credit Cards to UPI.

teacher_understanding.question: Which card–platform linkage is highlighted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page highlights linking RuPay credit cards to UPI.

teacher_understanding.question: Which card type is explicitly named in this innovation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Credit cards, not merely the RuPay debit cards mentioned in the preceding bullet.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the learner understand a card linked to UPI?
teacher_understanding.answer: UPI becomes the payment interface while the linked credit card is the funding source for eligible payments; interface and funding source are different layers.

items.exam_note: Do not generalise the line into universal eligibility for every card or every UPI transaction.

terms.term: linking RuPay Credit Cards to UPI
terms.plain_meaning: UPI से payment करते समय जुड़ा RuPay credit card इस्तेमाल करना
terms.everyday_image: QR payment के पीछे credit card का funding रास्ता

why_chain.step: A familiar payment interface can connect to different funding sources.
The page identifies RuPay credit-card linkage to UPI as an innovation.

unpack.example_or_place: An eligible merchant payment through UPI using a linked RuPay credit card.
unpack.consequence: Sets up the distinction between UPI as infrastructure and e-RUPI as a voucher built using it.
unpack.visual_verb: link credit card to UPI
unpack.level_extra: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface (outside clarification).

items.content: Vertical RuPay country graphic: six flag-and-country entries, top to bottom Bhutan, Nepal, Mauritius, United Arab Emirates, Singapore and Maldives. Each flag is paired with a country name and a statement about RuPay issuance or acceptance. There are no arrows or route connections.
items.type_note: The image proposal was none; this inset contains teachable visual country information.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the inset show?
teacher_understanding.answer: It pairs six countries with specific RuPay card issuance or acceptance claims.

teacher_understanding.question: Which countries appear?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bhutan, Nepal, Mauritius, United Arab Emirates, Singapore and Maldives.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should issuance and acceptance be read separately?
teacher_understanding.answer: Issuance means making cards available through an issuer; acceptance means allowing their use at supported payment or cash-access points. One does not automatically establish the other.

items.exam_note: Read country-specific wording; this is not a uniform claim of issuance in all six countries.

terms.plain_meaning: ग्राहक को नया card जारी करना
terms.everyday_image: bank से नया card मिलना

terms.plain_meaning: उस जगह card से लेन-देन हो पाना
terms.everyday_image: दुकान की machine पर card चल जाना

why_chain.step: A domestic card system may also have overseas use arrangements.
The inset gives different country-specific issuance and acceptance facts.

unpack.example_or_place: An Indian traveller checking supported overseas card facilities.
unpack.consequence: Domestic origin does not mean use is confined to India.
unpack.visual_verb: pair each flag with its distinct claim
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer acceptance at every outlet or treat the list as exhaustive or current.

items.where_on_page: right inset, first entry beside Bhutan flag
items.content: BHUTAN — First country to issue RuPay cards (2020). Accepted at ATMs and merchants.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinctive Bhutan claim does the inset make?
teacher_understanding.answer: It names Bhutan as the first country to issue RuPay cards in 2020 and states acceptance at ATMs and merchants.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are the date and acceptance channels given?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are printed in the first flag entry, beside Bhutan.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'first country' be understood in this international inset?
teacher_understanding.answer: As the overseas-issuance milestone in context, not a claim that RuPay originated in Bhutan rather than India.

items.exam_note: Pair Bhutan with the 2020 issuance milestone; avoid losing the overseas context.

why_chain.step: International reach can involve issuing cards as well as accepting them.
Bhutan's entry records both an issuance milestone and acceptance channels.

unpack.example_or_place: Bhutan: ATMs and merchants.
unpack.consequence: Differentiate this issuance milestone from Mauritius's 2024 entry.
unpack.visual_verb: pin 2020 to Bhutan
unpack.level_extra: Read the first-country claim in the foreign-country inset's context.

items.where_on_page: right inset, second entry beside Nepal flag
items.content: NEPAL — Accepted at ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What facilities are named for Nepal?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay acceptance at ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this entry give a Nepal card-issuance date?
teacher_understanding.answer: No; it gives acceptance channels, unlike the dated issuance entries.

teacher_understanding.question: How does PoS use differ from ATM use?
teacher_understanding.answer: A PoS terminal supports merchant payment, while an ATM provides banking functions such as cash withdrawal.

items.exam_note: Nepal is an acceptance entry, not a dated issuance entry.

terms.plain_meaning: दुकान पर card से payment लेने वाली machine
terms.everyday_image: किराने की दुकान की card machine

why_chain.step: Travellers need to know where a card can be used.
Nepal's entry identifies ATMs and PoS terminals.

unpack.example_or_place: Nepal, supported ATM or shop terminal.
unpack.consequence: Shows both cash-access and purchase-payment channels.
unpack.visual_verb: connect Nepal to ATM and shop icons
unpack.level_extra: PoS expands to Point of Sale (outside clarification).

items.where_on_page: right inset, third entry beside Mauritius flag
items.content: MAURITIUS — RuPay card issuance started in 2024.

teacher_understanding.question: What Mauritius milestone is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay card issuance started in 2024.

teacher_understanding.question: Is this entry about issuance or named acceptance locations?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly concerns card issuance and supplies a year, not a list of ATM or merchant channels.

teacher_understanding.question: Why not automatically add ATM acceptance to this entry?
teacher_understanding.answer: Issuance and acceptance are different claims, and evidence for one should not be treated as proof of every channel of the other.

items.exam_note: Match Mauritius with 2024, not Bhutan's 2020.

why_chain.step: Overseas development includes local issuance milestones.
The Mauritius entry dates issuance to 2024.

unpack.example_or_place: Mauritius, 2024 issuance milestone.
unpack.consequence: Adds a later date to the RuPay chronology.
unpack.visual_verb: pin 2024 to Mauritius
unpack.level_extra: Do not convert an issuance fact into an unstated universal acceptance claim.

items.where_on_page: right inset, fourth entry beside UAE flag
items.content: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES — Accepted at ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What acceptance channels are stated for the UAE?
teacher_understanding.answer: ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the UAE entry include an issuance year?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Its printed claim is acceptance at those two types of facilities.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a merchant terminal relate to card use?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the merchant-side device used to initiate and process a card payment.

items.exam_note: Country–acceptance matching fact.

why_chain.step: An overseas card user needs supported access points.
The UAE entry names ATMs and merchant terminals.

unpack.example_or_place: UAE, supported ATM or merchant terminal.
unpack.consequence: Extends the domestic system's stated overseas reach.
unpack.visual_verb: pair UAE flag with two acceptance icons
unpack.level_extra: Supported acceptance is not a promise that every terminal accepts the card.

items.where_on_page: right inset, fifth entry beside Singapore flag
items.content: SINGAPORE — Accepted at ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the Singapore acceptance claim?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay is accepted at ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other inset entry uses the same channel wording?
teacher_understanding.answer: The United Arab Emirates entry also says ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the channel wording important?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies where the card may be used rather than claiming that local card issuance has started.

items.exam_note: Do not attach Bhutan's or Mauritius's issuance dates to Singapore.

why_chain.step: Foreign use depends on acceptance arrangements.
Singapore's entry names ATM and merchant-terminal acceptance.

unpack.example_or_place: Singapore, supported ATM or merchant terminal.
unpack.consequence: Reinforces the acceptance-versus-issuance distinction.
unpack.visual_verb: pair Singapore with ATM and merchant icons
unpack.level_extra: Treat as the book's snapshot, not a live coverage guarantee.

items.where_on_page: right inset, last entry beside Maldives flag
items.content: MALDIVES — Accepted at ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What channels are named for Maldives?
teacher_understanding.answer: ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Which entry has the same channel wording?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nepal also lists ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: How should these two channels be distinguished?
teacher_understanding.answer: An ATM is a banking access device; a PoS terminal is used at a merchant to take payments.

items.exam_note: Maldives appears in the image even though it is absent from native text.

why_chain.step: Card users need both cash-access and shopping-payment information.

items.content: E-Rupi by NPCI (2021)

teacher_understanding.question: Which year and institution are attached to e-RUPI?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heading associates it with NPCI and 2021.

teacher_understanding.question: Why introduce a purpose-restricted electronic voucher?
teacher_understanding.answer: Such a voucher can direct funded assistance toward a specified service rather than provide unrestricted spending money.

items.exam_note: Link 2021 and NPCI to e-RUPI; do not confuse the name with a digital rupee.

why_chain.step: A sponsor may want to fund a particular service.
The following text presents e-RUPI as a person- and purpose-specific voucher.

unpack.example_or_place: The page's vaccination voucher example.
unpack.consequence: Moves from general payment infrastructure to targeted service delivery.
unpack.visual_verb: place e-RUPI at 2021
unpack.level_extra: Contrast the RuPay 2012 and e-RUPI 2021 dates.

items.where_on_page: first e-Rupi bullet and repeated first bullet near bottom
items.content: E-Rupi is an SMS /QR Code based Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher created by National Payment Corporation of India [National Payments Corporation of India] (NPCI) using its UPI Platform. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: What is e-RUPI according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a prepaid cashless electronic voucher delivered through SMS or QR code, created by NPCI using its UPI platform.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words establish the instrument and its delivery form?
teacher_understanding.answer: The definition calls it a 'Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher' and specifies 'SMS /QR Code'.

teacher_understanding.question: How do prepaid, cashless and electronic fit together?
teacher_understanding.answer: Prepaid means value is funded in advance; cashless means redemption does not require handing over cash; electronic means the entitlement is represented digitally rather than as a paper coupon.

items.exam_note: Separate the voucher from its delivery medium and underlying platform.

terms.plain_meaning: पहले से रकम तय किया हुआ digital coupon, जिससे cash दिए बिना तय सेवा ली जाए
terms.everyday_image: फोन पर आया पहले से paid service coupon

terms.plain_meaning: फोन के message या scan होने वाले code से voucher मिलना
terms.everyday_image: फोन पर message या चौकोर scan code

why_chain.step: A sponsor needs a way to deliver funded service entitlement.
E-RUPI supplies a prepaid electronic voucher through SMS or QR code.

unpack.example_or_place: A ₹1,000 vaccination voucher sent to a phone.
unpack.consequence: Using UPI infrastructure does not make the voucher itself an ordinary UPI app.
unpack.visual_verb: send funded voucher to phone
unpack.level_extra: Correct NPCI's expansion to National Payments Corporation of India; SMS is Short Message Service and QR is Quick Response (outside clarification).

items.where_on_page: second e-Rupi bullet and its repetition
items.content: It is not a payment app, bank transfer, or digital currency. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: Which three things is e-RUPI explicitly distinguished from?
teacher_understanding.answer: A payment app, a bank transfer and digital currency.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a restricted voucher differ from unrestricted account money or currency?
teacher_understanding.answer: A voucher represents an entitlement subject to stated redemption conditions rather than general spending power in the recipient's account or a currency instrument.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does an SMS or QR form not make it a payment app?
teacher_understanding.answer: SMS and QR describe delivery or presentation; an app is software used as an interface. The form in which an entitlement arrives does not determine its economic category.

items.exam_note: High-value statement trap: e-RUPI is not the digital rupee or a cryptocurrency.

why_chain.step: Similar digital names can hide different types of instruments.
The page excludes apps, bank transfers and digital currency from e-RUPI's definition.

unpack.example_or_place: A service coupon compared with money credited freely into an account.
unpack.consequence: Focus classification on what can be redeemed, not on the digital appearance.
unpack.visual_verb: separate voucher from app, transfer and currency
unpack.level_extra: Do not equate e-RUPI with e₹ merely because both names refer to the rupee.

items.where_on_page: third e-Rupi bullet and its repetition
items.content: Instead, it is a person-specific and purpose-specific voucher that can only be used by the intended beneficiary for the intended service. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: What two restrictions define e-RUPI here?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is tied to the intended beneficiary and to the intended service.

teacher_understanding.question: Which wording rules out general spending?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says 'person-specific and purpose-specific' and restricts use to the intended beneficiary and service.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are both restrictions needed for targeted assistance?
teacher_understanding.answer: A person restriction addresses who receives the benefit; a purpose restriction addresses what the benefit buys. Either alone leaves the other targeting question unresolved.

items.exam_note: Remember both axes: intended person AND intended purpose.

terms.plain_meaning: जिस व्यक्ति के लिए है, उसी के इस्तेमाल के लिए
terms.everyday_image: किसी एक नाम का service coupon

terms.plain_meaning: जिस काम के लिए मिला है, उसी काम में इस्तेमाल
terms.everyday_image: vaccination का coupon, grocery खरीदने का पैसा नहीं

why_chain.step: A sponsor may need to ensure both the right recipient and the right service.
E-RUPI is restricted on both person and purpose.

unpack.example_or_place: The intended beneficiary redeeming a vaccination voucher.
unpack.consequence: Explains why cash withdrawal or spending elsewhere is excluded in the example.
unpack.visual_verb: lock voucher to a person and a service
unpack.level_extra: The two restrictions are separate conditions, not synonyms.

items.content: Think of it as a digital gift coupon with restrictions. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: How does the gift-coupon analogy help explain e-RUPI?
teacher_understanding.answer: It makes the voucher understandable as a prepaid entitlement that is presented to obtain an allowed service.

teacher_understanding.question: What limits the ordinary gift-coupon analogy?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page specifies person and purpose restrictions; it is not describing an unrestricted gift of spending money.

teacher_understanding.question: Why keep the word 'restrictions' in the analogy?
teacher_understanding.answer: Without it, learners might incorrectly assume that the recipient can spend the value on any purchase or pass it around freely.

items.exam_note: Useful memory aid, but the formal restrictions determine correctness.

terms.plain_meaning: फोन वाला coupon, पर इस्तेमाल की तय शर्तों के साथ
terms.everyday_image: एक खास सेवा के लिए मिला coupon

why_chain.step: An unfamiliar digital instrument needs a familiar everyday comparison.
The page uses a restricted digital gift coupon as that comparison.

unpack.example_or_place: A coupon that pays for a service but cannot be converted into shopping cash.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the learner for the numerical vaccination example.
unpack.visual_verb: transform gift coupon into restricted digital voucher
unpack.level_extra: An analogy explains the idea; it does not remove beneficiary or purpose conditions.

items.where_on_page: indented vaccination example and partial repeated example at bottom
items.content: Suppose the government wants to pay for your COVID vaccination costing ₹1,000. Instead of transferring ₹1,000 into your bank account, it sends you an e-RUPI voucher worth ₹1,000 via SMS or QR code. You can redeem it only for vaccination at an authorized center—not withdraw cash or spend it elsewhere. The first two sentences are repeated at the bottom of this page; the repeated redemption sentence continues on the next page.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the vaccination example work?
teacher_understanding.answer: The government funds a ₹1,000 vaccination benefit, sends a voucher of that value through SMS or QR code instead of crediting the recipient's account, and the beneficiary redeems it for vaccination at an authorised centre.

teacher_understanding.question: When and where may the beneficiary use the voucher in this example?
teacher_understanding.answer: When obtaining the specified vaccination at an authorised centre; the example excludes cash withdrawal and unrelated spending.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does sending a ₹1,000 voucher differ from transferring ₹1,000 to an account?
teacher_understanding.answer: The voucher constrains the use of the funded benefit, whereas an ordinary unrestricted account credit does not itself impose that vaccination-only redemption condition.

teacher_understanding.question: Is ₹1,000 a general e-RUPI limit or an announced universal vaccination benefit?
teacher_understanding.answer: No such rule is stated. The text begins 'Suppose', making ₹1,000 the illustrative cost and voucher value in this example.

items.exam_note: ₹ means Indian rupees; ₹1,000 is illustrative, not a stated statutory limit. Do not treat the example as an actual scheme announcement.

terms.plain_meaning: voucher दिखाकर उसके बदले तय सेवा लेना
terms.everyday_image: vaccination centre पर coupon देकर सेवा लेना

terms.plain_meaning: वह centre जहाँ इस voucher के बदले सेवा लेने की अनुमति है
terms.everyday_image: तय centre पर coupon मान्य होना

why_chain.step: The government in the hypothetical example wants to pay for vaccination, not unrelated purchases.
It sends a ₹1,000 voucher redeemable only for vaccination at an authorised centre.

unpack.example_or_place: Government → ₹1,000 SMS/QR voucher → intended beneficiary → authorised vaccination centre.
unpack.consequence: Shows person-and-purpose targeting in action and why a voucher is not unrestricted cash.
unpack.visual_verb: send voucher, redeem service, block cash and unrelated purchases
unpack.level_extra: Track sponsor, beneficiary, value, delivery medium, provider and permitted use separately.
